signature.name: Vasa Museum
signature.detail: Home to the nearly intact 1628 warship Vasa, the world's best-preserved 17th-century ship. A must-see for maritime history and engineering. Tip: book tickets online and visit early morning or late afternoon to avoid crowds.

signature.name: Gamla Stan
signature.detail: Stockholm's old town is a maze of cobblestone streets, colorful 17th-century buildings, and the Royal Palace. It's the historic heart of the city. Tip: wear comfortable shoes and explore early to enjoy quiet streets.

signature.name: Stockholm Palace
signature.detail: One of Europe's largest royal palaces, still the official residence of the Swedish monarch. See the state apartments and changing of the guard. Tip: check the guard ceremony schedule (usually midday) and buy tickets in advance.

signature.name: Stockholm City Hall
signature.detail: Famous for the Blue Hall (Nobel Prize banquet) and the Golden Hall mosaics. Guided tours are the only way inside. Tip: book a guided tour online; climb the tower in summer for views.

signature.name: Skansen
signature.detail: The world's oldest open-air museum, with historic buildings and a zoo showcasing Swedish life. A family favorite. Tip: allow at least half a day; visit on a weekday for fewer crowds.

signature.name: ABBA The Museum
signature.detail: Interactive museum dedicated to Sweden's pop legends, with memorabilia and sing-along fun. Tip: book timed tickets online; it's next to Gröna Lund on Djurgården.

signature.name: Stockholm Metro Art
signature.detail: Over 90 stations feature art installations, often called the world's longest art gallery. The Blue Line's T-Centralen and Solna Centrum are highlights. Tip: use a single-journey ticket or travel card to hop between stations.
